words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the clause as showing the benefit of obligatory duties and urging believers to spend capacity beyond them on voluntary worship and good works, a recommendation called nadb.
rows.anchor: ferâizden mâ‘adâ tetavvu‘ât ve nevâfile teşvîki mutazammındır ki buna “nedb” tâbir olunur

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second construal says properly directed effort earns benefit, while blind striving after harm costs the person; capacity-calibrated divine duties guide people toward benefit and away from loss.
rows.anchor: Her nefsin kazandığı, yani yoluyla isteyip isâbet ettiği menfaatine, aksine veya kör körüne çalışıp boğuştuğu zararınadır.

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without duties people would be idle, while demands beyond capacity would waste effort; either result would mean God did not will His servants’ good, contrary to the mercy of the Compassionate.
rows.anchor: Her iki surette Allah kullarının hayrını istememiş, zararlarını istemiş olurdu ki bu da Rahmân-ı Rahîm’in rahmetine münâfîdir.

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, both occurrences of “what” may denote good: benefit actually attained and good that was not attained; even blind, fruitless striving wastes effort and may lead to worse harm.
rows.anchor: Her iki ما hayırdan ibaret olabilir ki biri ele geçen hayır, biri de ele geçmeyen hayırdır.

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third construal treats gains made for oneself and others as truly in one’s own favor, while selfish gain driven by appetite harms the self, since even earning depends on other people; divine duty reconciles self-interest and altruism.
rows.anchor: Asıl kazanç böyle kazançtır ki hayır buna derler.

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth construal says one’s own earnings secure rights and benefit, whereas living on another’s earnings is against oneself; duties protect people from dependence and secure rights through charity and fair exchange, while forbidding begging, usury, and aggression.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah infâk-ı hayır, mübâdele-i sahîha teklif etmiş, tese’’ülden, ribâdan, tecavüzden nehy eylemiştir.

words: لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes favor the first construal and attach the others to it; Elmalılı calls that first reading the main explanation because it is clear and contains the secrets of divine obligation.
rows.anchor: Ekseriyetle müfessirîn bu dört mânadan birincisi üzerine yürümüşler, berikilerin her birini birer vechile ona ilhak eylemişlerdir.

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s answer to the believers’ plea calms their anxiety through ease and relief, making Qur’anic recitation a direct dialogue and intimate prayer for the Prophet and his community; Elmalılı compares this style with al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: Bu, Kur’an okuyan veya dinleyen mü’minlerin ara sıra kendilerini Cenâb-ı Allah ile bizzat mükâleme hâlinde bulmaları gibi büyük bir ni‘met-i intâkı tazammun eder.

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the response is separated by a pause, it is phrased as if the believers themselves were voicing it: they would immediately accept and repeat the promised ease because it matches their own hopes.
rows.anchor: yine onların sözleri ve onlardan hikâye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lists three parses: everything from “we heard and obeyed” to the surah’s end is governed by “they said”; the assurance in 2:286 is parenthetical within that speech; or an unexpressed “say” introduces the supplications.
rows.anchor: Bunun için burada nahiv nokta-i nazarından üç vecih vardır.

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petitions are taught as the close of the believers’ earlier prayers, without an explicit command to say them; their opening renews resolve to obey while fearing disobedience.
rows.anchor: şimdi de şöyle deyiniz diye emir tasrih olunmayarak bu da evvelki dualarının âhiri suretinde tâlim buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: A qudsi hadith cited here says the believing servant continues drawing near to God through supererogatory acts, supporting the exhortation to spend surplus capacity in good works.
rows.anchor: لاَ يَزَالُ عَبْدِى الْمُؤْمِنُ يَتَقَرَّبُ إِلَيَّ بِالنَّوَافِلِ hadîs-i kudsîsi

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first plea asks that the community not be punished in this world or the next for unintentional omission or error: despite renewed resolve, generic liability for what one acquires could include a forgotten duty or unintended prohibited act.
rows.anchor: وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ ise mutlak olduğundan bunlardan muâhaze muhtemildir.

words: رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetfulness and error fall into two kinds: some may excuse the person, while others do not, because a person can be responsible for failing to take reasonable precautions.
rows.anchor: Nisyan ve Hata İki Nevidir: Birisi sâhibi mâzur görülebilir, diğerinde görülmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who notices impurity on clothing but delays removing it and later forgets before praying is not excused, because the initial delay was negligent; someone who never noticed it is excused.
rows.anchor: bir kimse üzerinde bir necaset görse de izâlesini tehir eylese, sonra unutup namaz kılsa mâzur olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hunter who shoots without checking whether a person may be present, then hits someone, is not excused because he failed to take the necessary care.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik bir kimse bir ava tüfek atsa da bir insanı vursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who fails to learn religious and legal duties, or fails to review them after learning them, is not excused for later forgetting; some causes of forgetfulness are within human capacity to prevent.
rows.anchor: insan vezâif-i dîniye ve şer‘iyesini bellemeye çalışmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Involuntary error does not change the intrinsic harm or unlawfulness of the resulting act, just as swallowed poison remains harmful or an accidental fall into a well remains dangerous; people must avoid such outcomes as far as possible.
rows.anchor: hiç nisyan ve hata yapmamak vüs‘-i beşerden hâriç de olsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some legal duties remain in error cases such as accidental killing, and forgetfulness or error does not remove compensation for harm to other people; the plea seeks freedom from punishment, not freedom from obligation, including for causes and consequences.
rows.anchor: Nisyan ve hata hukūk-ı ‘ibâddaki zararın damânına mâni‘olmaz.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Elmalılı relates the plea to the Prophetic hadith, “My community’s error and forgetfulness are lifted,” while preserving liability for harm to others.
rows.anchor: Nitekim رُفِعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي اَلْخَطَأُ وَالنِّسْيَان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isr is a heavy burden or bond that holds the bearer in place, associated with captivity and confinement; it can also refer to a weighty covenant, subjection, the womb, and kinship.
rows.anchor: “Isr”, asl-ı lügatta esr ü habs mânasıyla alâkadar olup altındakini yerinde tutan ağır yük ve bağ demektir

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: müfessirîn
rows.claim: Exegetes describe severe requirements imposed on earlier peoples, especially Jews: fifty daily prayers, a quarter of property as tax, cutting away impurity on clothing, exile, swift executions, self-killing for repentance, immediate punishment for rebellion, and prohibition of some lawful foods after an error.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin beyanlarına nazaran meselâ Yahudîler günde elli vakit namaz kılmak, malının dörtte birini vergi vermek

words: كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا
rows.speaker: Kaffâl
rows.claim: Kaffal says the fifth book claimed as Torah contains further examples of the Jews’ harsh laws; believers prayed for protection from such severity, which God later removed, as 7:157 states.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Kaffâl’de demiştir ki: “Yahudîlerin ellerinde Tevrat

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The petition remains necessary because wusʿ, though broader than capacity, is also commonly used for capacity; a burden proportionate to capacity may still be severe, so the prayer asks God to make the apparent sense one of ease.
rows.anchor: vüs‘, tâkatten geniş ise de tâkat mânasına isti‘mâli de meşhurdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actions can be broader than divine legislation: oppressive conditions may come as discipline through tyrants such as Pharaoh acting against God’s law. The verb “load” allows for this, and the surah’s Israelite stories have signaled both sources of hardship.
rows.anchor: Bunun için حمل tâbir olunmuştur.

words: رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea covers unbearable burdens whether legal, which may drive people to revolt, or existential, which become torment and destruction; God could impose such things as a test or punishment, so believers ask for protection in every form.
rows.anchor: olursa yapılamaz, isyan ve ihtilâle sevk eder, tekvînî olursa ta‘zîb olur

words: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance of ease is glad tidings for Muhammad’s community, whose faith, obedience, sincerity, sound will, and adherence to truth suit this gift; unbelievers do not escape duty and instead impose desire-driven, unjust demands on one another.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا tebşîrin ümmet-i Muhammededir.

words: وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community’s law is a divinely imposed burden: believers receive a straight law as mercy, while unbelievers receive a crooked one as the effect of justice and wrath; what counts as justice differs with their spiritual condition, and God turns hearts, so the plea asks for steadfastness in Islam.
rows.anchor: mü’minlerinki müstakīm ve eser-i rahmet, kâfirlerinki gayr-i müstakīm ve eser-i adl ü gazabdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pardon us” asks God to erase the effects of sins. People pledge sincere obedience but still fall short, cannot fully spend the God-given capacity and will in His path, and therefore ask through grace rather than earned merit; though deeds remain in divine knowledge, God can remove their consequences.
rows.anchor: Fakat Sen kemâl-i kudretinle onların bize müteveccih olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains forgiveness as covering and concealing people’s faults, suppressing their blemishes, and not exposing them publicly.
rows.anchor: bize mağfiret de et, ayıplarımızı ilm-i ilâhînde gizle, ört, bastır, eller içinde bizi rüsvây eyleme.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for mercy asks God to bestow blessings on the petitioners.
rows.anchor: rahmetinle bize in‘âm da et

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlana means our patron, owner and master, guardian of our affairs, and helper; Elmalılı links it to the declaration that God is the protector of those who believe.
rows.anchor: Sen bizim mevlâmız, sâhib ü mâlikimiz, veliyy-i umûrumuz, nâsırımızsın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers ask for material and spiritual victory over unbelievers in defending the truth and raising God’s word.
rows.anchor: maddeten, mânen müdafa‘a-i hak ve i‘lâ-yı kelimede bizi gālib ve muzaffer eyle.

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Muslim and Tirmidhi report that when the Prophet prayed with these petitions, God answered, “So I have done.”
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz bu dualarla dua ettiği zaman taraf-ı ilâhîden “peki yaptım” buyurulduğu Müslim ve Tirmizî’de rivayet edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the forthcoming Sura of Al-i Imran begins as a response to this prayer for victory.
rows.anchor: bu nusret duasına bir cevap olarak başlayacaktır.

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
rows.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn Masud, included in the Kutub al-Sitta, says whoever recites the last two verses of al-Baqara at night will find them sufficient.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan rivayet olunan bir hadîs-i nebevîde buyurulmuştur ki “her kim geceleyin Sûretü’l-Bakara’dan iki âyeti okursa ona kifayet eder.”

rows.speaker: Ebû Zer
rows.claim: Abu Dharr’s report, cited by Hakim and Bayhaqi, says the Prophet received the surah’s final two verses from a treasure beneath the Throne and urged people to learn and teach them as prayer, Qur’an, and supplication.
rows.anchor: Ebû Zer’den tahrîc ettikleri diğer bir hadîs-i şerîfte de Fahr-ı Risâlet buyurmuştur ki: “Allah teâlâ Sûre-i Bakara’yı iki âyetle hitâma erdirdi

rows.speaker: Ömer ve Ali
rows.claim: Both Umar and Ali are reported to have said that they knew no sensible person who went to sleep without reciting these final verses of al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer ile Hazret-i Ali radıyallahu ‘anhümâ’dan mervîdir ki her biri “âkil bir adam görmezdim ki Sûre-i Bakara’nın âhirindeki bu âyetleri okumadan uyusun

rows.speaker: Ebû Meysere
rows.claim: Abu Maysara reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet to say “amen” at the end of Sura al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: “Cibrîl Resûlullah’a Sûre-i Bakara’nın âhirinde ‘âmîn’ telkin etti” diye de Ebû Meysere’den mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı closes by praying that God grant worshippers a great share of the promised response when they understand these supplications and follow what they require.
rows.anchor: bu duaların mânalarını fehm ve muktezâsına ittibâ‘ile vaad ettiği feyz-i icâbetinden büyük büyük nasiblerle kâmyâb buyursun.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering of the vow, Elmalılı calls Imran’s wife his “harem” and renders the unborn child as dedicated to God “free of every restriction.”
rows.anchor: İmrân’ın haremi dediği vakit: “Yâ Rabbi! Ben karnımdakini her kayıttan âzâde olarak Sana adadım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report names Jesus’ maternal grandmother, Imran’s wife, as Hanne bint Fakuza; Hanne’s sister—or, in another report, Maryam’s sister—was Iysha, wife of Zakariya and mother of Yahya. The Prophet is reported to call Yahya and Jesus cousins, sons of maternal aunts.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Hazret-i Îsâ’nın ninesi zevce-i İmrân’ın ismi “Hanne binti Fâkuza”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muharrar means thoroughly freed or made free; it is explained as a sincere worshipper, a temple servant, or someone freed from worldly concerns.
rows.anchor: “Muharrer”: Esâsen iyice azadlanmış, hâlis hür yapılmış demektir ki ibadette muhlis veya mabed hâdimi veya dünyadan âzade mânalarıyla tefsir edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihrab normally means the mosque’s front place where the imam stands; by part-for-whole usage it can mean the mosque, and it can also name its most honored, foremost place.
rows.anchor: mescidlerin ön tarafında imamın duracağı mevki‘-i mahsustur. Zikr-i cüz, irâde-i kül tarîkiyle mescide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here Elmalılı takes mihrab to mean a raised chamber in the mosque, reached by stairs, where Zakariya placed Maryam and kept her under his care.
rows.anchor: burada “mihrab”dan murad, mescidde merdivenle çıkılır bir mahfil olduğu beyan ediliyor ki Hazret-i Meryem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam, orphaned from her father while still in the womb, was born with a sacred spiritual nature and received special divine nurture in the mihrab.
rows.anchor: rahm-i mâderde babasından yetim kalan Hazret-i Meryem böyle kudsî bir rûhâniyetle doğmuş ve böyle bir mihrabda min ‘indillah mazhariyyet-i mahsûsa ile perverişyâb olmuştu.

words: ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muhammad was not present when the people cast lots over Maryam’s care or disputed, Elmalılı treats this account of the unseen as proof that Muhammad is the true, divinely revealed Messenger whom people must obey.
rows.anchor: senin vâcibu’l-itâ‘a bir Resûl-i Kibriyâ Muhammed Mustafâ olduğunda ve bu haberlerin vahy-i hak bulunduğunda şüphe yok.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this reminder about the unseen and the dispute over Maryam’s selection, the narrative is to continue by recounting the full truth of Jesus’ story.
rows.anchor: Bu ihtar akabinde ve ihtisâm noktasında ıstıfâ-yı Meryem’e müte‘allik olarak Îsâ kıssasının dahi bütün hakikatini anlatmak için şunları yâd et:
